claims.text: The investigated alloy has the composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Conventionally cast Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits extensive non-eutectic primary crystallization during cooling.
The alloy undergoes multistep crystallization upon reheating.
An inert mold coating such as boron nitride or yttria-stabilized zirconia should be applied during casting.
The proposed mold coating will reduce heterogeneous nucleation sites at the alloy-mold interface.
Reducing heterogeneous nucleation sites will suppress initiation of primary crystallization.
Suppressing primary crystallization will preserve a larger amorphous fraction.
The coating prevents direct contact between the alloy melt and the mold.
The coating reduces the energy barriers for nucleation.
The coating minimizes contamination- or inhomogeneity-induced nucleation.
The coating produces a more uniform temperature profile during cooling.
The coating delays the onset of crystallization during cooling or reheating.
Coated-mold samples will retain a larger amorphous fraction than uncoated-mold samples.
Coated-mold samples will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature during reheating than uncoated samples.
A higher reheating crystallization-onset temperature represents enhanced thermal stability.
The coating will improve amorphous retention at cooling rates slower than those required by the uncoated system.
Some amorphous phase is observed in the uncoated alloy under rapid cooling.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes suppression of nucleation to the coating, but the mechanism says that the coating reduces the energy barrier for nucleation. Lowering a nucleation barrier ordinarily facilitates nucleation, so this statement conflicts with the claimed reduction in heterogeneous nucleation and delayed crystallization.
